chunks: And the weak will say to the arrogant: 'Not in the least. It was your plotting night and day when you ordered us to disbelieve in God and associate compeers with Him.' When they see the punishment they will express repentance. But We shall put iron collars round the necks of infidels. Will they be requited for anything but what they did?
ai.seo_question: How do the weak and arrogant disbelievers interact on the Day of Judgment according to Surah Saba?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological shift on the Day of Judgment where the 'weak' (al-mustad'afun) initially blame the 'arrogant' (al-mustakbirun) for their misguidance, only for both parties to realize that the leaders' plotting was merely a mechanism of divine decree. The imagery of iron collars (aghlaal) symbolizes the inescapable nature of their own deeds, reinforcing the principle that ultimate accountability rests on individual agency despite external influence. This interaction underscores the transition from passive following to active regret, illustrating the futility of excuses when the reality of divine justice becomes manifest.
